scope: Authored fictional teaching cases. No messages were sent, no real recipients were studied, and no probability is fitted to app data. The routing, reply-count, utility and pressure cases are separate fixtures.

messages.requires: No shared hobby claim; intentionally little context.

messages.text: You mentioned board games. Co-op or competitive? No pressure to reply.
messages.requires: A supplied recipient board-games quote, plus Alex's existing board-games fact.

messages.text: Hi, I'm Alex. I'd like to get to know you. Fine to pass.
messages.requires: Alex's supplied intent; no claim about the recipient's interests.

messages.text: Is this a co-op campaign or a competitive matchmaking queue? Fine to pass.
messages.requires: Even with a board-games quote, understanding the campaign/queue joke is not supplied.

replyScope: Two disjoint groups of ten invented matched conversations, each with one assigned opener, one exposure and a completed 48-hour observation window. Any inbound reply, including a decline, counts once. No random allocation is supplied.
utilityScope: Independent decision exercise. Probabilities 0.20 and 0.40 are assumed inputs, not validated estimates from the tiny reply fixture. Costs count composition time only; value and time price are arbitrary utility units.
pressureScope: A separate counterexample to maximising any reply. Categories describe authored response content, not feelings. Counts are fabricated, not outcomes of a real intervention or the two-group reply fixture.
